paper.title: IR Lens: A Tool for Interpreting Cross-Encoder Models
paper.abstract: Transformer-based ranking models, such as MonoBERT, are central to Information Retrieval; yet their inner workings remain largely opaque. This hinders not only our understanding of the systems implementing them, but also our ability to improve them. To alleviate this limitation, we introduce IR Lens, a new interpretability tool tailored to cross-encoders based on two key components: 1) Neuron Integrated Gradients to expose the contributions of model parts at multiple levels, and 2) targeted ablations to support hypothesis tracking. With its interactive graphical interface, IR Lens enables IR practitioners to explore, analyze, and manipulate neuron-level mechanisms in cross-encoders, facilitating a deeper understanding of neural ranking models. By extending the reach of existing interpretability methods, we believe IR Lens has the potential to support the improvement of cross-encoders.
